summary: The staged LuaPad probe's public temporary state.stop callback is dot-call safe but does not normalize colon-call or arbitrary reason arguments. Cleanup is performed, then a table concatenation can raise or an unexpected caller-provided string can appear in terminal chat output.

reproducer.setup: Standalone synthetic Inspect.Time.Frame, Inspect.Tooltip, Command.Event.Attach/Detach and Event.System.Update.Begin; no RIFT API/client invoked.

behavior.observed: Implicit state table used as reason; one detachment and state clearing occurred, then status string concatenation raised an error.
No exception; unexpected caller-supplied string appears in terminal notice.

fix_contract: Normalize public state.stop arguments for either dot or colon invocation.
Map unknown argument types, arbitrary status strings and nil to a fixed allowed CANCELLED reason before passing to complete().
Preserve exact handler detachment, done state, cache and quarantine behavior.
Extend synthetic fixture with both negative controls; rerun genuine Lua 5.1 and existing hash-pinned Lua 5.3 gates.
integrity_note: Do not change the source while its SHA is pinned in the LuaPad guide, preview20 note, session handoff, offline runner defaults and accepted Lua5.1 receipt. Treat the source fix and reference/hash migration as one reviewed integration.
scope_limit: Defensive static/synthetic reproducibility only; documented operator snippet uses dot syntax. No physical in-game failure has been observed.
